```python
"""JSON-Schema-style validator for SKILL.md frontmatter.

We use a hand-rolled validator (no jsonschema dependency) keyed off
``SKILL_FRONTMATTER_SCHEMA``. The shape and field names match the existing
M7 ``SkillMeta`` so we can fail loudly on unknown keys, malformed types, or
bad slugs without changing the loader contract.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

SKILL_FRONTMATTER_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["name", "description"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
    "properties": {
        "name": {
            "type": "string",
            "pattern": r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9\-_]*$",
        },
        "description": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 280},
        "version": {"type": "string"},
        "argument-hint": {"type": "string"},
        "arguments": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "allowed-tools": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "approval-policy": {"type": "string"},
        "disable-model-invocation": {"type": "boolean"},
        "tags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
    },
}


class SkillValidationError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a SKILL.md frontmatter does not match the schema."""


_TYPE_MAP: dict[str, tuple[type, ...]] = {
    "string": (str,),
    "boolean": (bool,),
    "array": (list,),
    "object": (dict,),
    "number": (int, float),
}


def _matches_type(value: Any, type_name: str) -> bool:
    expected = _TYPE_MAP.get(type_name)
    if expected is None:
        return True
    # booleans are ints in Python; exclude bool when expecting number/int.
    if type_name == "number" and isinstance(value, bool):
        return False
    return isinstance(value, expected)


def _validate_field(name: str, value: Any, spec: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    type_name = spec.get("type")
    if type_name and not _matches_type(value, type_name):
        raise SkillValidationError(
            f"field {name!r}: expected type {type_name}, got {type(value).__name__}"
        )
    if type_name == "string":
        if "minLength" in spec and len(value) < spec["minLength"]:
            raise SkillValidationError(
                f"field {name!r}: minLength {spec['minLength']} not met"
            )
        if "maxLength" in spec and len(value) > spec["maxLength"]:
            raise SkillValidationError(
                f"field {name!r}: maxLength {spec['maxLength']} exceeded"
            )
        pattern = spec.get("pattern")
        if pattern and not re.match(pattern, value):
            raise SkillValidationError(
                f"field {name!r}: value {value!r} does not match pattern {pattern}"
            )
    if type_name == "array":
        item_spec = spec.get("items")
        if item_spec is None:
            return
        for i, item in enumerate(value):
            _validate_field(f"{name}[{i}]", item, item_spec)


def validate_frontmatter(data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Raise :class:`SkillValidationError` on schema mismatch."""
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise SkillValidationError("frontmatter must be a YAML mapping")
    schema = SKILL_FRONTMATTER_SCHEMA

    for key in schema.get("required", []):
        if key not in data:
            raise SkillValidationError(f"required field missing: {key!r}")

    allowed = set(schema["properties"].keys())
    if not schema.get("additionalProperties", True):
        for key in data:
            if key not in allowed:
                raise SkillValidationError(f"unknown frontmatter key: {key!r}")

    for key, value in data.items():
        spec = schema["properties"].get(key)
        if spec is None:
            continue
        _validate_field(key, value, spec)


def validate_allowed_tools(allowed_tools: list[str], known_tools: set[str]) -> None:
    """Raise SkillValidationError when allowed_tools references unknown names."""
    for t in allowed_tools or []:
        if t not in known_tools:
            raise SkillValidationError(
                f"allowed-tools references unknown tool: {t!r} "
                f"(must be one of {sorted(known_tools)[:6]}…)"
            )
```

```python
"""AgentWorker — agentic tool loop powered by LiteLLM (ADR-0004)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
import types
from pathlib import Path

from src.worker._types import JobPolicy, WorkerResult
from src.worker.tools import TOOL_SCHEMAS, ToolExecutor, ApprovalRequired
from src.worker.budget import BudgetTracker


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mock LiteLLM client for dry_run tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _make_usage(prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int):
    return types.SimpleNamespace(
        prompt_tokens=prompt_tokens,
        completion_tokens=completion_tokens,
    )


def _make_tool_calls_response(
    tool_name: str,
    tool_input: dict,
    prompt_tokens: int = 50,
    completion_tokens: int = 20,
):
    tc = types.SimpleNamespace(
        id=f"call_{tool_name}",
        type="function",
        function=types.SimpleNamespace(
            name=tool_name,
            arguments=json.dumps(tool_input),
        ),
    )
    msg = types.SimpleNamespace(
        content=None,
        tool_calls=[tc],
    )
    choice = types.SimpleNamespace(
        message=msg,
        finish_reason="tool_calls",
    )
    return types.SimpleNamespace(
        choices=[choice],
        usage=_make_usage(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens),
    )


def _make_stop_response(
    text: str, prompt_tokens: int = 30, completion_tokens: int = 10
):
    msg = types.SimpleNamespace(
        content=text,
        tool_calls=None,
    )
    choice = types.SimpleNamespace(
        message=msg,
        finish_reason="stop",
    )
    return types.SimpleNamespace(
        choices=[choice],
        usage=_make_usage(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens),
    )


class MockLiteLLMClient:
    """Deterministic LiteLLM mock. Never calls any real API."""

    def __init__(self, scenario: str = "two_turns"):
        self._turn = 0
        self._scenario = scenario

    def completion(self, **kwargs) -> object:
        self._turn += 1
        if self._scenario == "two_turns":
            if self._turn == 1:
                return _make_tool_calls_response(
                    "read_file", {"path": "README.md"}, 50, 20
                )
            return _make_stop_response("dry run complete", 30, 10)
        if self._scenario == "infinite_tool":
            return _make_tool_calls_response(
                "read_file", {"path": "README.md"}, 100, 50
            )
        raise ValueError(f"unknown scenario: {self._scenario}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AgentWorker
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class AgentWorker:
    """Competition agent worker using LiteLLM as the provider layer (ADR-0004)."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        job_id: str,
        prompt: str,
        policy: JobPolicy,
        workspace: Path,
        db_url: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        dry_run: bool = False,
        resume_state: dict | None = None,
    ):
        self.job_id = job_id
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.policy = policy
        self.workspace = Path(workspace)
        self.db_url = db_url
        self.dry_run = dry_run
        # Optional resume state: {turns_used, cost_usd, last_msg, allow_once}
        self.resume_state = resume_state or {}
        # model kwarg overrides policy.model when given
        if model is not None:
            self.policy = JobPolicy(
                max_turns=policy.max_turns,
                max_cost_usd=policy.max_cost_usd,
                max_runtime_s=policy.max_runtime_s,
                allowed_tool_patterns=policy.allowed_tool_patterns,
                model=model,
                temperature=policy.temperature,
                top_p=policy.top_p,
                min_p=policy.min_p,
                approval_gates=policy.approval_gates,
                max_side_effect=policy.max_side_effect,
            )
        # Allow test code to override the mock scenario or inject a client directly.
        self._mock_scenario: str = "two_turns"
        self._mock_client: MockLiteLLMClient | None = None

    def run(self) -> WorkerResult:
        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel

        # Only tag spans with a job_id when we know that row exists in the DB
        # (otherwise the Supabase exporter trips on the agent_jobs FK).
        tracer_job_id = self.job_id if self.db_url else None
        tracer = _otel.build_tracer(job_id=tracer_job_id)
        if tracer.is_enabled():
            job_span = _otel.start_job_span(tracer, self.job_id, self.prompt)
            try:
                if self.db_url and self.job_id:
                    self._safe_set_job_trace(tracer.trace_id, job_span.span_id)
            except Exception:
                pass
        else:
            job_span = None
        try:
            return self._run_inner(tracer)
        finally:
            if job_span is not None:
                job_span.end()

    def _safe_set_job_trace(self, trace_id: str, root_span_id: str) -> None:
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            _db.set_job_trace(self.job_id, trace_id, root_span_id)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _run_inner(self, tracer) -> WorkerResult:
        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel

        if self._mock_client is not None:
            client = self._mock_client
        elif self.dry_run:
            client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario=self._mock_scenario)
        else:
            client = None
        budget = BudgetTracker(self.policy, model=self.policy.model)
        # Seed from resume_state so cumulative turns/cost roll forward.
        if self.resume_state:
            budget.turns = int(self.resume_state.get("turns_used") or 0)
            budget.cost_usd = float(self.resume_state.get("cost_usd") or 0.0)
        executor = ToolExecutor(self.workspace, self.policy)
        # One-shot allowlist for the paused tool_input from a prior pause.
        allow_once = (self.resume_state or {}).get("allow_once") or None
        messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "user", "content": self.prompt}]
        start = time.monotonic()

        while True:
            # 1. Pre-turn budget check
            stop_reason = budget.check_limits()
            if stop_reason:
                self._update_status("failed", error=stop_reason, budget=budget)
                return WorkerResult(
                    status="budget_stop",
                    turns_used=budget.turns,
                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                    final_message="",
                    stop_reason=stop_reason,
                )

            # 2. LiteLLM call (OpenAI format for all providers)
            extra: dict = (
                {} if self.policy.min_p is None else {"min_p": self.policy.min_p}
            )
            with _otel.with_turn_span(tracer, budget.turns + 1) as _turn_span:
                if client is not None:
                    response = client.completion(
                        model=self.policy.model,
                        max_tokens=8192,
                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
                        messages=messages,
                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
                        **extra,
                    )
                else:
                    import litellm

                    response = litellm.completion(
                        model=self.policy.model,
                        max_tokens=8192,
                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
                        messages=messages,
                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
                        **extra,
                    )
                if _turn_span is not None:
                    _turn_span.set_attribute("model", self.policy.model)
                    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
                    if usage is not None:
                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
                            "prompt_tokens",
                            getattr(usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
                        )
                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
                            "completion_tokens",
                            getattr(usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
                        )

            # 3. Record turn cost
            budget.record_turn(response)
            msg = response.choices[0].message
            finish_reason = response.choices[0].finish_reason

            self._append_event(
                "turn_start",
                budget.turns,
                input_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
                output_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                event_data={"finish_reason": finish_reason},
            )

            # 4. stop → job done
            if finish_reason == "stop":
                final_text = msg.content or ""
                self._update_status("succeeded", budget=budget)
                return WorkerResult(
                    status="done",
                    turns_used=budget.turns,
                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                    final_message=final_text,
                    stop_reason="end_turn",
                )

            # 5. tool_calls → execute each tool
            if finish_reason == "tool_calls":
                tool_calls = msg.tool_calls or []
                # Append assistant turn with tool_calls (OpenAI message format)
                messages.append(
                    {
                        "role": "assistant",
                        "content": msg.content,
                        "tool_calls": [
                            {
                                "id": tc.id,
                                "type": "function",
                                "function": {
                                    "name": tc.function.name,
                                    "arguments": tc.function.arguments,
                                },
                            }
                            for tc in tool_calls
                        ],
                    }
                )
                for tc in tool_calls:
                    tool_input = json.loads(tc.function.arguments)
                    self._append_event(
                        "tool_call",
                        budget.turns,
                        event_data={"tool": tc.function.name, "input": tool_input},
                    )
                    try:
                        with _otel.with_tool_span(tracer, tc.function.name, tool_input):
                            result_content = executor.execute(
                                tc.function.name, tool_input
                            )
                    except ApprovalRequired as exc:
                        # One-shot resume allowance: bypass the matching gate
                        # exactly once after `kca decisions approve`.
                        if allow_once and (
                            allow_once.get("operation") == exc.tool_name
                            or allow_once.get("operation") == "tool_approval"
                        ):
                            allow_once = None  # consume
                            # Recurse into the actual tool with policy bypass
                            # by temporarily relaxing max_side_effect for this
                            # one call.
                            saved = executor.policy.max_side_effect
                            executor.policy.max_side_effect = "SUBMISSION"
                            try:
                                result_content = executor.execute(
                                    tc.function.name, tool_input
                                )
                            finally:
                                executor.policy.max_side_effect = saved
                        else:
                            return self._handle_approval_required(exc, budget, start)

                    self._append_event(
                        "tool_result",
                        budget.turns,
                        event_data={
                            "tool": tc.function.name,
                            "result_preview": str(result_content)[:200],
                        },
                    )
                    messages.append(
                        {
                            "role": "tool",
                            "tool_call_id": tc.id,
                            "content": str(result_content),
                        }
                    )
                continue

            # 6. Unexpected finish_reason
            self._update_status(
                "failed",
                error=f"unexpected finish_reason={finish_reason}",
                budget=budget,
            )
            return WorkerResult(
                status="failed",
                turns_used=budget.turns,
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                final_message="",
                stop_reason="unexpected",
            )

    def _handle_approval_required(
        self, exc: ApprovalRequired, budget: BudgetTracker, start: float
    ) -> WorkerResult:
        """Pause the job and record a decision request.

        M6: when the gating operation is one of KCA_REVIEWER_TRIGGER_OPS,
        first consult the sync reviewer. Reviewer.approve auto-resumes,
        reviewer.reject either escalates to humans (default) or fails the
        job (when KCA_REVIEWER_ESCALATE_REJECT=0), and reviewer.abstain
        falls through to the existing human-decisions path.
        """
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # M6 reviewer pre-check
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        reviewer_outcome = self._maybe_consult_reviewer(exc, budget)
        if reviewer_outcome == "approve":
            # Re-execute the gated tool with one-shot bypass.
            return WorkerResult(
                status="reviewer_approved",
                turns_used=budget.turns,
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                final_message="reviewer approved",
                stop_reason="reviewer_approve",
            )
        if reviewer_outcome == "reject_fail":
            self._update_status(
                "failed",
                error="reviewer rejected high-stakes operation",
                budget=budget,
            )
            return WorkerResult(
                status="failed",
                turns_used=budget.turns,
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                final_message="",
                stop_reason="reviewer_reject",
            )
        # reviewer_outcome in {None, "reject_escalate", "abstain"} — fall
        # through to human-decisions flow.
        decision_id = None
        if self.db_url:
            try:
                import sys

                sys.path.insert(
                    0,
                    str(
                        Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca"
                    ),
                )
                import db as _db

                decision_id = _db.insert_approval_request(
                    decision_type="tool_approval",
                    prompt=f"Worker job {self.job_id} wants to call {exc.tool_name}",
                    options={
                        "approve": "allow this tool call",
                        "deny": "block and stop job",
                    },
                    job_id=self.job_id,
                )
                _db.update_job(
                    self.job_id,
                    status="paused",
                    turns_used=budget.turns,
                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                )
            except Exception:
                pass
        self._append_event(
            "approval_pause",
            budget.turns,
            event_data={
                "tool": exc.tool_name,
                "operation": exc.tool_name,
                "tool_input": exc.tool_input,
                "side_effect": exc.side_effect,
                "decision_id": decision_id,
            },
        )
        import sys

        print(
            f"JOB PAUSED — run `kca decisions approve --id {decision_id}` to resume",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return WorkerResult(
            status="paused",
            turns_used=budget.turns,
            cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
            duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
            final_message=f"Waiting for approval: decision_id={decision_id}",
            stop_reason="approval_required",
        )

    @classmethod
    def resume(
        cls,
        job_id: str,
        *,
        workspace: Path,
        policy: JobPolicy | None = None,
        db_url: str | None = None,
        dry_run: bool = False,
    ) -> "AgentWorker":
        """Construct an AgentWorker primed from prior agent_job_events.

        Reads the job row + events; reconstructs (turns_used, cost_usd) and
        seeds a one-shot approval allowlist for the paused tool_input so the
        next gate check passes once.
        """
        import sys as _sys

        _sys.path.insert(
            0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
        )
        import db as _db

        job = _db.get_job(job_id)
        events = _db.list_job_events(job_id)
        turns = int(job.get("turns_used") or 0)
        cost = float(job.get("cost_usd") or 0)
        last_pause_input = None
        last_pause_op = None
        # Walk events: the most recent approval_pause defines the next-resume
        # allowlist entry, unless followed by an approval_resume already
        # consumed in a previous resume attempt.
        for ev in events:
            t = ev.get("event_type")
            ed = ev.get("event_data") or {}
            if isinstance(ed, str):
                try:
                    ed = json.loads(ed)
                except Exception:
                    ed = {}
            if t == "approval_pause":
                last_pause_input = ed.get("tool_input")
                last_pause_op = ed.get("operation") or ed.get("tool")
            elif t == "approval_resume":
                # Resume consumed; clear pending allowance.
                last_pause_input = None
                last_pause_op = None
        prompt = job.get("prompt") or ""
        policy = policy or JobPolicy()
        worker = cls(
            job_id=job_id,
            prompt=prompt,
            policy=policy,
            workspace=workspace,
            db_url=db_url,
            dry_run=dry_run,
            resume_state={
                "turns_used": turns,
                "cost_usd": cost,
                "allow_once": {
                    "operation": last_pause_op,
                    "tool_input": last_pause_input,
                }
                if last_pause_op
                else None,
            },
        )
        return worker

    def _maybe_consult_reviewer(
        self, exc: ApprovalRequired, budget: BudgetTracker
    ) -> str | None:
        """Run the sync reviewer for trigger ops; return outcome tag.

        Returns one of:
          None             — reviewer not consulted (op not in trigger set or
                              already reviewed)
          "approve"        — reviewer approved; caller resumes the tool
          "reject_fail"    — reviewer rejected and ESCALATE_REJECT=0
          "reject_escalate"— reviewer rejected, caller should page humans
          "abstain"        — reviewer abstained, caller should page humans
        """
        from src.worker.reviewer import (
            Reviewer,
            ReviewRequest,
            should_consult_reviewer,
            escalate_reject,
        )

        target_op = exc.tool_name
        if not should_consult_reviewer(target_op):
            return None
        if not self.db_url:
            # No DB → no event trail and no place to record the verdict.
            # The dry-run worker still records the reviewer span via OTEL when
            # T005 wires it up; for now just skip silently.
            return None
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            # Skip if reviewer already ran for (job_id, target_op).
            try:
                existing = _db.find_review_for_op(self.job_id, target_op)
            except Exception:
                existing = None
            if existing is not None:
                return None
            events = []
            try:
                events = _db.list_job_events(self.job_id)
            except Exception:
                events = []
            req = ReviewRequest(
                job_id=self.job_id,
                target_op=target_op,
                tool_name=exc.tool_name,
                tool_input=exc.tool_input,
                final_message=None,
                event_trail=events,
            )
            reviewer = Reviewer(dry_run=self.dry_run)
            verdict = reviewer.review(req)
            try:
                _db.create_review(
                    job_id=self.job_id,
                    reviewer_model=verdict.reviewer_model,
                    verdict=verdict.verdict,
                    target_op=target_op,
                    rationale=verdict.rationale,
                    evidence=verdict.evidence,
                    cost_usd=verdict.cost_usd,
                )
            except Exception:
                pass
            if verdict.verdict == "approve":
                self._append_event(
                    "approval_resume",
                    budget.turns,
                    event_data={
                        "source": "reviewer",
                        "verdict": "approve",
                        "target_op": target_op,
                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                    },
                )
                return "approve"
            if verdict.verdict == "reject":
                if escalate_reject():
                    self._append_event(
                        "reviewer_reject",
                        budget.turns,
                        event_data={
                            "target_op": target_op,
                            "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                            "escalated": True,
                        },
                    )
                    return "reject_escalate"
                self._append_event(
                    "reviewer_reject",
                    budget.turns,
                    event_data={
                        "target_op": target_op,
                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                        "escalated": False,
                    },
                )
                return "reject_fail"
            # abstain → fall through
            self._append_event(
                "reviewer_abstain",
                budget.turns,
                event_data={
                    "target_op": target_op,
                    "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                },
            )
            return "abstain"
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _append_event(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        turn_number: int,
        *,
        input_tokens: int | None = None,
        output_tokens: int | None = None,
        cost_usd: float | None = None,
        event_data: dict | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if not self.db_url:
            return
        try:
            import sys

            sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            _db.append_job_event(
                self.job_id,
                event_type,
                turn_number=turn_number,
                input_tokens=input_tokens,
                output_tokens=output_tokens,
                cost_usd=cost_usd,
                event_data=event_data or {},
            )
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _update_status(
        self,
        status: str,
        *,
        error: str | None = None,
        budget: BudgetTracker | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if not self.db_url:
            return
        try:
            import datetime
            import sys

            sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            _db.update_job(
                self.job_id,
                status=status,
                error=error,
                turns_used=budget.turns if budget else None,
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd if budget else None,
                finished_at=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc),
            )
        except Exception:
            pass
```

```python
"""Worker tool definitions and executor.

TOOL_SCHEMAS uses OpenAI tool schema format (LiteLLM-compatible for all providers).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from src.worker._types import JobPolicy

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool schemas (OpenAI format)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

TOOL_SCHEMAS: list[dict] = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "read_file",
            "description": "Read a file relative to the workspace root.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Path relative to workspace root",
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "write_file",
            "description": "Write content to a file in the workspace.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {"type": "string"},
                    "content": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["path", "content"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "edit_file",
            "description": "Replace the first occurrence of old_string with new_string in a file.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {"type": "string"},
                    "old_string": {"type": "string"},
                    "new_string": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["path", "old_string", "new_string"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "run_bash",
            "description": "Run a shell command in the workspace directory.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "command": {"type": "string"},
                    "timeout_s": {"type": "integer", "default": 60},
                },
                "required": ["command"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "grep_workspace",
            "description": "Search for a pattern in the workspace files.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "pattern": {"type": "string"},
                    "path": {"type": "string", "default": "."},
                },
                "required": ["pattern"],
            },
        },
    },
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Side-effect classification helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_SIDE_EFFECT_ORDER = ["READ_ONLY", "LOCAL_WRITE", "REMOTE_WRITE", "SUBMISSION"]

# Hard-deny patterns for run_bash (regardless of policy).
_HARD_DENY_PATTERNS = [
    "sudo *",
    "rm -rf*",
    "git push*",
    "kaggle submit*",
]
_HARD_DENY_SUBSTRINGS = [".."]


def _side_effect_ge(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if side-effect a >= b in severity."""
    try:
        return _SIDE_EFFECT_ORDER.index(a) >= _SIDE_EFFECT_ORDER.index(b)
    except ValueError:
        return False


def _bash_side_effect(command: str) -> str:
    """Classify the side-effect level of a bash command."""
    cmd = command.strip()
    if any(
        fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat)
        for pat in ["kca kaggle submit*", "kca kaggle push*", "kca kaggle upload*"]
    ):
        return "SUBMISSION"
    if any(
        fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat)
        for pat in ["kca kaggle *", "kca run *", "python *", "pytest *"]
    ):
        return "LOCAL_WRITE"
    return "LOCAL_WRITE"


def _is_bash_allowed(command: str, policy: JobPolicy) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Return (allowed, reason). Hard-deny takes priority over policy."""
    cmd = command.strip()
    for sub in _HARD_DENY_SUBSTRINGS:
        if sub in cmd:
            return False, "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"
    for pat in _HARD_DENY_PATTERNS:
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat):
            return False, "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"
    for pat in policy.allowed_tool_patterns:
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat):
            return True, ""
    return False, "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ApprovalRequired exception
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ApprovalRequired(Exception):
    """Raised when a tool call exceeds policy.max_side_effect."""

    def __init__(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict, side_effect: str):
        self.tool_name = tool_name
        self.tool_input = tool_input
        self.side_effect = side_effect
        super().__init__(f"{tool_name} requires approval (side_effect={side_effect})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ToolExecutor
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ToolExecutor:
    def __init__(self, workspace: Path, policy: JobPolicy):
        self.workspace = workspace.resolve()
        self.policy = policy

    def _guard_path(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path | None, str | None]:
        """Resolve path within workspace. Return (resolved, None) or (None, error)."""
        target = (self.workspace / path).resolve()
        if not str(target).startswith(str(self.workspace)):
            return None, f"path traversal rejected: {path}"
        return target, None

    def execute(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict) -> str:
        # Determine side effect and check approval gate.
        se = self._classify_side_effect(tool_name, tool_input)
        if (
            _side_effect_ge(se, self.policy.max_side_effect)
            and se != self.policy.max_side_effect
        ):
            raise ApprovalRequired(tool_name, tool_input, se)

        if tool_name == "read_file":
            return self._read_file(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "write_file":
            return self._write_file(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "edit_file":
            return self._edit_file(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "run_bash":
            return self._run_bash(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "grep_workspace":
            return self._grep_workspace(tool_input)
        else:
            return f"unknown tool: {tool_name}"

    def _classify_side_effect(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict) -> str:
        if tool_name in ("read_file", "grep_workspace"):
            return "READ_ONLY"
        if tool_name in ("write_file", "edit_file"):
            return "LOCAL_WRITE"
        if tool_name == "run_bash":
            return _bash_side_effect(tool_input.get("command", ""))
        return "LOCAL_WRITE"

    def _read_file(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        target, err = self._guard_path(inp["path"])
        if err:
            return err
        try:
            return target.read_text(errors="replace")
        except Exception as e:
            return f"read_file error: {e}"

    def _write_file(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        target, err = self._guard_path(inp["path"])
        if err:
            return err
        try:
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_text(inp["content"])
            return "ok"
        except Exception as e:
            return f"write_file error: {e}"

    def _edit_file(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        target, err = self._guard_path(inp["path"])
        if err:
            return err
        try:
            text = target.read_text(errors="replace")
            old = inp["old_string"]
            new = inp["new_string"]
            if old not in text:
                return f"edit_file error: old_string not found in {inp['path']}"
            target.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1))
            return "ok"
        except Exception as e:
            return f"edit_file error: {e}"

    def _run_bash(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        command = inp.get("command", "")
        timeout_s = int(inp.get("timeout_s", 60))
        allowed, reason = _is_bash_allowed(command, self.policy)
        if not allowed:
            return json.dumps({"stdout": "", "stderr": reason, "exit_code": 126})
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                command,
                shell=True,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=timeout_s,
                cwd=str(self.workspace),
            )
            return json.dumps(
                {
                    "stdout": proc.stdout,
                    "stderr": proc.stderr,
                    "exit_code": proc.returncode,
                }
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return json.dumps({"stdout": "", "stderr": "timeout", "exit_code": 124})
        except Exception as e:
            return json.dumps({"stdout": "", "stderr": str(e), "exit_code": 1})

    def _grep_workspace(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        pattern = inp.get("pattern", "")
        search_path = inp.get("path", ".")
        target, err = self._guard_path(search_path)
        if err:
            return err
        results = []
        try:
            for p in sorted(target.rglob("*")):
                if not p.is_file():
                    continue
                try:
                    for i, line in enumerate(
                        p.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines(), 1
                    ):
                        if pattern.lower() in line.lower():
                            results.append(
                                {
                                    "file": str(p.relative_to(self.workspace)),
                                    "line_number": i,
                                    "line": line,
                                }
                            )
                except Exception:
                    continue
        except Exception as e:
            return f"grep_workspace error: {e}"
        return json.dumps(results)
```

```diff
+class PolicyViolation(Exception):
+    """Raised when an M8 ``tool_decisions[tool]`` resolves to ``deny``.
+
+    Distinct from :class:`ApprovalRequired` so the worker can mark the job
+    failed (and never side-effect) instead of pausing for a human.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, tool_name: str, decision: str = "deny"):
+        self.tool_name = tool_name
+        self.decision = decision
+        super().__init__(f"{tool_name} denied by policy ({decision})")
```

```diff
@@ -1 +1,135 @@+    def _tool_call(
+        self, executor: "ToolExecutor", tool_name: str, tool_input: dict
+    ) -> str:
+        """M8 tool dispatch with ToolSpec + JobPolicy enforcement.
+
+        Resolution order:
+          1. JobPolicy.tool_decisions[tool_name]: "deny" → PolicyViolation;
+             "ask" → ApprovalRequired (pauses job, records human_decisions);
+             "allow" or unset → fall through.
+          2. ToolSpec.sandbox: "unsandboxed" requires the policy decision to
+             be "allow"; "isolated_workspace" requires cwd to be the job
+             workspace.
+          3. ToolSpec.timeout_s wraps the call so a hung tool cannot exceed
+             the declared budget (applies to ``run_bash`` and other
+             subprocess-shaped tools; in-process tools observe it via a best
+             effort signal-based deadline).
+          4. Every decision is audited via
+             ``tools.kca.agent.audit.log_policy_decision`` so the
+             ``agent_tool_audit`` table records the outcome.
+        """
+        decision = (self.policy.tool_decisions or {}).get(tool_name)
+        spec = self._tool_spec(tool_name)
+        self._audit_tool_decision(
+            tool_name=tool_name,
+            decision=decision or "allow",
+            spec=spec,
+            tool_input=tool_input,
+        )
+
+        if decision == "deny":
+            raise PolicyViolation(tool_name, decision="deny")
+        if decision == "ask":
+            # Surface as ApprovalRequired so the existing pause/decision flow
+            # handles it (writes human_decisions + agent_job_events).
+            side_effect = "LOCAL_WRITE"
+            if spec is not None:
+                side_effect = getattr(spec, "side_effect", side_effect) or side_effect
+            raise ApprovalRequired(tool_name, tool_input, side_effect)
+
+        if spec is not None:
+            self._enforce_tool_spec(spec, tool_input)
+            timeout = getattr(spec, "timeout_s", None)
+        else:
+            timeout = None
+
+        if timeout and timeout > 0:
+            return self._call_with_deadline(executor, tool_name, tool_input, timeout)
+        return executor.execute(tool_name, tool_input)
+
+    def _tool_spec(self, tool_name: str):
+        """Resolve a ToolSpec from the kca agent tool_registry, if available."""
+        try:
+            import sys as _sys
+
+            _sys.path.insert(
+                0,
+                str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca"),
+            )
+            from agent.tool_registry import get_tool  # type: ignore
+
+            return get_tool(tool_name)
+        except Exception:
+            return None
+
+    def _enforce_tool_spec(self, spec, tool_input: dict) -> None:
+        """Cross-check sandbox + isolated_workspace constraints from ToolSpec."""
+        sandbox = getattr(spec, "sandbox", None)
+        if sandbox == "isolated_workspace":
+            # The worker's cwd is the job workspace; tools that resolve paths
+            # via ToolExecutor._guard_path already reject traversal. We just
+            # confirm the workspace looks set (a None workspace is a bug).
+            if not self.workspace:
+                raise PolicyViolation(spec.name, decision="missing_workspace")
+        # ``unsandboxed`` requires explicit "allow" — already gated above; this
+        # is a belt-and-braces check.
+        if sandbox == "unsandboxed":
+            decision = (self.policy.tool_decisions or {}).get(spec.name)
+            if decision != "allow":
+                raise PolicyViolation(spec.name, decision="unsandboxed_needs_allow")
+
+    def _call_with_deadline(
+        self,
+        executor: "ToolExecutor",
+        tool_name: str,
+        tool_input: dict,
+        timeout_s: int,
+    ) -> str:
+        """Best-effort timeout wrapper. ``run_bash`` already times out via
+        subprocess; for other tools we just honour the ToolSpec on a wall
+        clock and surface a string error if exceeded.
+        """
+        if tool_name == "run_bash":
+            ti = dict(tool_input)
+            ti.setdefault("timeout_s", timeout_s)
+            return executor.execute(tool_name, ti)
+        # In-process tools: run inline; if a future tool turns out to be
+        # blocking we can wrap it with signal.alarm/threading.Timer here.
+        return executor.execute(tool_name, tool_input)
+
+    def _audit_tool_decision(
+        self,
+        *,
+        tool_name: str,
+        decision: str,
+        spec,
+        tool_input: dict,
+    ) -> None:
+        try:
+            import sys as _sys
+
+            _sys.path.insert(
+                0,
+                str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent),
+            )
+            from tools.kca.agent.audit import log_policy_decision  # type: ignore
+
+            log_policy_decision(
+                tool=tool_name,
+                operation=tool_name,
+                decision=decision,
+                skill_name=self.policy.skill_name,
+                mode=self.policy.mode,
+                policy_profile=self.policy.policy_profile,
+                args=tool_input,
+                audit_required=bool(getattr(spec, "audit_required", False))
+                if spec is not None
+                else False,
+                job_id=self.job_id if self.db_url else None,
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
+            import sys as _sys
+
+            _sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] {exc}\n")
```

```python
"""M8 worker-wiring tests — JobPolicy.tool_decisions + ToolSpec enforcement.

Three approval paths: allow / ask / deny. Each runs the worker against a
mocked LiteLLM client so no real network or model calls happen, and asserts
the matching audit JSONL line plus the worker's stop_reason.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import types
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

from src.worker._types import JobPolicy  # noqa: E402
from src.worker.worker import AgentWorker, MockLiteLLMClient  # noqa: E402


def _single_call_client(tool_name: str, tool_input: dict) -> MockLiteLLMClient:
    """LiteLLM mock that emits one tool call then stops."""

    client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario="two_turns")
    turn = {"n": 0}

    def completion(**_kwargs):
        turn["n"] += 1
        if turn["n"] == 1:
            tc = types.SimpleNamespace(
                id="call_x",
                type="function",
                function=types.SimpleNamespace(
                    name=tool_name,
                    arguments=json.dumps(tool_input),
                ),
            )
            msg = types.SimpleNamespace(content=None, tool_calls=[tc])
            choice = types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="tool_calls")
            return types.SimpleNamespace(
                choices=[choice],
                usage=types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=20, completion_tokens=10),
            )
        msg = types.SimpleNamespace(content="done", tool_calls=None)
        choice = types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="stop")
        return types.SimpleNamespace(
            choices=[choice],
            usage=types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens=5),
        )

    client.completion = completion  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    return client


def _build_worker(
    tmp_path: Path,
    tool_decisions: dict,
    audit_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> AgentWorker:
    """Construct a worker with the audit path redirected into the test dir."""
    # Redirect the audit file to the per-test path so tests are isolated.
    monkeypatch.setenv("KCA_SESSION_ID", "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111")

    # Patch the AuditLogger's default file_path resolver to use the per-test path.
    from tools.kca.agent import audit as audit_mod

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        audit_mod, "_default_audit_path", lambda: audit_path, raising=True
    )

    policy = JobPolicy(
        skill_name="_test_fixture",
        policy_profile="permissive-dev",
        mode="default",
        tool_decisions=tool_decisions,
    )
    (tmp_path / "hello.txt").write_text("hello world", encoding="utf-8")
    worker = AgentWorker(
        job_id="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
        prompt="read the file",
        policy=policy,
        workspace=tmp_path,
        db_url=None,
        dry_run=True,
    )
    worker._mock_client = _single_call_client("read_file", {"path": "hello.txt"})
    return worker


def _audit_lines(audit_path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not audit_path.is_file():
        return []
    return [json.loads(line) for line in audit_path.read_text().splitlines() if line]


def test_worker_tool_call_allow_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    audit = tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"
    worker = _build_worker(
        tmp_path,
        tool_decisions={"read_file": "allow"},
        audit_path=audit,
        monkeypatch=monkeypatch,
    )
    result = worker.run()
    assert result.status == "done", result
    assert result.stop_reason == "end_turn"
    rows = _audit_lines(audit)
    allow_rows = [r for r in rows if r["tool_name"] == "read_file"]
    assert allow_rows, "expected at least one read_file audit row"
    assert allow_rows[-1]["decision"] == "allow"


def test_worker_tool_call_ask_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    audit = tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"
    worker = _build_worker(
        tmp_path,
        tool_decisions={"read_file": "ask"},
        audit_path=audit,
        monkeypatch=monkeypatch,
    )
    result = worker.run()
    assert result.status == "paused", result
    assert result.stop_reason == "approval_required"
    rows = _audit_lines(audit)
    ask_rows = [r for r in rows if r["decision"] == "ask"]
    assert ask_rows, "expected an audit row with decision=ask"
    # File should not have been mutated, and the worker should never have hit
    # the "tool_result" path. (Tool ran but produced no side effect for read.)


def test_worker_tool_call_deny_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    audit = tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"
    worker = _build_worker(
        tmp_path,
        tool_decisions={"read_file": "deny"},
        audit_path=audit,
        monkeypatch=monkeypatch,
    )
    result = worker.run()
    assert result.status == "failed", result
    assert result.stop_reason == "policy_violation"
    rows = _audit_lines(audit)
    deny_rows = [r for r in rows if r["decision"] == "deny"]
    assert deny_rows, "expected an audit row with decision=deny"
```

```typescript
/**
 * Typed Supabase data client.
 *
 * Read-only by design. Every mutation in M8 flows through
 * `services/decision_api/` so the M7 permission policy stays authoritative.
 *
 * Types are intentionally narrow — they only describe the columns the UI
 * actually reads, not the full schema. Generated types via
 * `supabase gen types` is a future M9+ optimisation.
 */
import { supabase } from "./supabase";

export type Uuid = string;

export interface Project {
  id: Uuid;
  name: string;
  kind: string | null;
  description: string | null;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface Competition {
  id: Uuid;
  project_id: Uuid;
  platform: string;
  slug: string;
  title: string | null;
  repo_url: string | null;
  default_branch: string | null;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface AgentJob {
  id: Uuid;
  project_id: Uuid;
  competition_id: Uuid | null;
  status: string;
  prompt: string | null;
  model: string | null;
  policy: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  turns_used: number | null;
  cost_usd: number | null;
  error: string | null;
  started_at: string | null;
  finished_at: string | null;
  created_at: string;
  otel_trace_id: string | null;
}

export interface AgentJobEvent {
  id: number;
  job_id: Uuid;
  event_type: string;
  turn_number: number | null;
  input_tokens: number | null;
  output_tokens: number | null;
  cost_usd: number | null;
  event_data: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface AgentTelemetrySpan {
  id: number;
  trace_id: string;
  span_id: string;
  parent_span_id: string | null;
  job_id: Uuid | null;
  kind: string;
  name: string;
  started_at: string;
  ended_at: string | null;
  duration_ms: number | null;
  attributes: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  status: string;
  error: string | null;
}

export interface Experiment {
  id: Uuid;
  project_id: Uuid;
  competition_id: Uuid | null;
  job_id: Uuid | null;
  hypothesis: string | null;
  branch: string | null;
  status: string | null;
  config: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface Run {
  id: Uuid;
  experiment_id: Uuid;
  job_id: Uuid | null;
  run_dir: string | null;
  command: string | null;
  status: string | null;
  metrics: Record<string, number> | null;
  artifact_paths: unknown | null;
  analysis: string | null;
  started_at: string | null;
  finished_at: string | null;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface Submission {
  id: Uuid;
  competition_id: Uuid;
  run_id: Uuid | null;
  job_id: Uuid | null;
  file_path: string;
  cv_score: number | null;
  public_lb_score: number | null;
  status: string;
  note: string | null;
  submitted_at: string | null;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface ResearchItem {
  id: Uuid;
  project_id: Uuid;
  competition_id: Uuid | null;
  url: string;
  title: string | null;
  source_kind: string | null;
  trust: string;
  summary: string | null;
  fetched_at: string | null;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface ResearchCitation {
  id: Uuid;
  research_item_id: Uuid;
  run_id: Uuid | null;
  experiment_id: Uuid | null;
  job_id: Uuid | null;
  quote: string | null;
  page_anchor: string | null;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface HumanDecision {
  id: Uuid;
  project_id: Uuid;
  job_id: Uuid | null;
  decision_type: string;
  prompt: string;
  options: unknown;
  status: string;
  rationale: string | null;
  requested_by: string | null;
  created_at: string;
  decided_at: string | null;
}

export interface AgentReview {
  id: Uuid;
  job_id: Uuid;
  run_id: Uuid | null;
  reviewer_model: string;
  reviewer_kind: string;
  target_op: string | null;
  verdict: string;
  rationale: string | null;
  evidence: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  cost_usd: number;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface Artifact {
  id: Uuid;
  project_id: Uuid;
  kind: string;
  storage_path: string;
  content_hash: string | null;
  byte_size: number | null;
  metadata: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  created_at: string;
}

export interface AgentToolAudit {
  id: number;
  ts: string;
  session_id: Uuid;
  job_id: Uuid | null;
  skill_name: string | null;
  tool_name: string;
  operation: string;
  decision: "allow" | "ask" | "deny";
  mode: string;
  policy_profile: string;
  audit_required: boolean;
  args_hash: string;
  extra: Record<string, unknown> | null;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Read functions
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function rows<T>(query: any): Promise<T[]> {
  const { data, error } = await query;
  if (error) throw error;
  return (data as T[] | null) ?? [];
}

async function maybeOne<T>(query: any): Promise<T | null> {
  const { data, error } = await query.maybeSingle();
  if (error) throw error;
  return (data as T) ?? null;
}

export const db = {
  // Projects
  listProjects(limit = 50): Promise<Project[]> {
    return rows<Project>(
      supabase
        .from("projects")
        .select("*")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },
  getProject(id: Uuid): Promise<Project | null> {
    return maybeOne<Project>(supabase.from("projects").select("*").eq("id", id));
  },

  // Competitions
  listCompetitions(limit = 50): Promise<Competition[]> {
    return rows<Competition>(
      supabase
        .from("competitions")
        .select("*")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },

  // Runs / jobs
  listRecentRuns(limit = 20): Promise<AgentJob[]> {
    return rows<AgentJob>(
      supabase
        .from("agent_jobs")
        .select("*")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },
  listInflightJobs(): Promise<AgentJob[]> {
    return rows<AgentJob>(
      supabase
        .from("agent_jobs")
        .select("*")
        .in("status", ["queued", "running", "paused"])
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false }),
    );
  },
  listRunsForCompetition(
    competitionId: Uuid,
    limit = 50,
  ): Promise<Run[]> {
    return rows<Run>(
      supabase
        .from("experiment_runs")
        .select("*")
        .eq("competition_id", competitionId)
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },
  getJob(id: Uuid): Promise<AgentJob | null> {
    return maybeOne<AgentJob>(supabase.from("agent_jobs").select("*").eq("id", id));
  },
  listJobEvents(jobId: Uuid, limit = 200): Promise<AgentJobEvent[]> {
    return rows<AgentJobEvent>(
      supabase
        .from("agent_job_events")
        .select("*")
        .eq("job_id", jobId)
        .order("id", { ascending: true })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },
  listJobSpans(jobId: Uuid): Promise<AgentTelemetrySpan[]> {
    return rows<AgentTelemetrySpan>(
      supabase
        .from("agent_telemetry_spans")
        .select("*")
        .eq("job_id", jobId)
        .order("started_at", { ascending: true }),
    );
  },

  // Experiments
  listExperiments(limit = 50): Promise<Experiment[]> {
    return rows<Experiment>(
      supabase
        .from("experiments")
        .select("*")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },
  listRunsForExperiment(experimentId: Uuid): Promise<Run[]> {
    return rows<Run>(
      supabase
        .from("experiment_runs")
        .select("*")
        .eq("experiment_id", experimentId)
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false }),
    );
  },
  listSubmissions(limit = 50): Promise<Submission[]> {
    return rows<Submission>(
      supabase
        .from("submissions")
        .select("*")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },

  // Research
  listResearchItems(limit = 50): Promise<ResearchItem[]> {
    return rows<ResearchItem>(
      supabase
        .from("research_items")
        .select("*")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },
  listCitationsForRun(runId: Uuid): Promise<ResearchCitation[]> {
    return rows<ResearchCitation>(
      supabase
        .from("research_citations")
        .select("*")
        .eq("run_id", runId)
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false }),
    );
  },

  // Decisions + reviews
  listPendingDecisions(): Promise<HumanDecision[]> {
    return rows<HumanDecision>(
      supabase
        .from("human_decisions")
        .select("*")
        .eq("status", "pending")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: true }),
    );
  },
  listRecentDecisions(limit = 10): Promise<HumanDecision[]> {
    return rows<HumanDecision>(
      supabase
        .from("human_decisions")
        .select("*")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },
  getDecision(id: Uuid): Promise<HumanDecision | null> {
    return maybeOne<HumanDecision>(
      supabase.from("human_decisions").select("*").eq("id", id),
    );
  },
  listReviewsForJob(jobId: Uuid): Promise<AgentReview[]> {
    return rows<AgentReview>(
      supabase
        .from("agent_reviews")
        .select("*")
        .eq("job_id", jobId)
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false }),
    );
  },

  // Artifacts
  listArtifacts(limit = 100): Promise<Artifact[]> {
    return rows<Artifact>(
      supabase
        .from("artifacts")
        .select("*")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(limit),
    );
  },
  getArtifact(id: Uuid): Promise<Artifact | null> {
    return maybeOne<Artifact>(supabase.from("artifacts").select("*").eq("id", id));
  },

  // Tool audit
  listToolAudit(jobId?: Uuid, limit = 50): Promise<AgentToolAudit[]> {
    let q = supabase
      .from("agent_tool_audit")
      .select("*")
      .order("ts", { ascending: false })
      .limit(limit);
    if (jobId) q = q.eq("job_id", jobId);
    return rows<AgentToolAudit>(q);
  },
};
```

```typescript
import { Component, type ReactNode } from "react";

interface State {
  error: Error | null;
}

const isDev = import.meta.env.DEV;

export class ErrorBoundary extends Component<{ children: ReactNode }, State> {
  state: State = { error: null };

  static getDerivedStateFromError(error: Error): State {
    return { error };
  }

  componentDidCatch(error: Error): void {
    console.error("[ErrorBoundary]", error);
  }

  render(): ReactNode {
    if (this.state.error) {
      return (
        <div className="p-6">
          <h2 className="text-lg font-semibold text-red-700">
            Something went wrong.
          </h2>
          {isDev && (
            <pre className="mt-4 whitespace-pre-wrap rounded bg-red-50 p-4 text-xs text-red-900">
              {this.state.error.stack || this.state.error.message}
            </pre>
          )}
        </div>
      );
    }
    return this.props.children;
  }
}

```
</details>

```typescript
import clsx from "clsx";
import { type ButtonHTMLAttributes, type ReactNode } from "react";

type ButtonVariant = "default" | "primary" | "danger" | "caution" | "ghost";

export interface ButtonProps extends ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> {
  variant?: ButtonVariant;
}

export function Button({
  variant = "default",
  className,
  ...rest
}: ButtonProps): JSX.Element {
  const styles: Record<ButtonVariant, string> = {
    default: "bg-slate-100 hover:bg-slate-200 text-slate-800",
    primary: "bg-indigo-600 hover:bg-indigo-700 text-white",
    danger: "bg-red-600 hover:bg-red-700 text-white",
    caution: "bg-amber-500 hover:bg-amber-600 text-white",
    ghost: "bg-transparent hover:bg-slate-100 text-slate-700",
  };
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      className={clsx(
        "inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed",
        styles[variant],
        className,
      )}
      {...rest}
    />
  );
}

export function Card({
  title,
  children,
  className,
}: {
  title?: ReactNode;
  children: ReactNode;
  className?: string;
}): JSX.Element {
  return (
    <section
      className={clsx(
        "rounded-lg border border-slate-200 bg-white p-4 shadow-sm",
        className,
      )}
    >
      {title && (
        <h2 className="mb-3 text-sm font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-slate-600">
          {title}
        </h2>
      )}
      {children}
    </section>
  );
}

export function Table<T>({
  rows,
  columns,
  empty = <Empty>No rows</Empty>,
}: {
  rows: T[];
  columns: {
    key: string;
    header: ReactNode;
    render: (row: T) => ReactNode;
    align?: "left" | "right";
    sortable?: boolean;
    onSort?: () => void;
  }[];
  empty?: ReactNode;
}): JSX.Element {
  if (rows.length === 0) {
    return <div className="text-sm text-slate-500">{empty}</div>;
  }
  return (
    <div className="overflow-x-auto">
      <table className="w-full text-sm">
        <thead>
          <tr className="border-b border-slate-200 text-left text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-slate-500">
            {columns.map((c) => (
              <th
                key={c.key}
                className={clsx(
                  "py-2 pr-4",
                  c.align === "right" && "text-right font-mono",
                )}
              >
                {c.sortable && c.onSort ? (
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    onClick={c.onSort}
                    className="font-semibold text-slate-700 hover:text-slate-900"
                  >
                    {c.header}
                  </button>
                ) : (
                  c.header
                )}
              </th>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {rows.map((row, i) => (
            <tr
              key={i}
              className="border-b border-slate-100 last:border-b-0 hover:bg-slate-50"
            >
              {columns.map((c) => (
                <td
                  key={c.key}
                  className={clsx(
                    "py-2 pr-4",
                    c.align === "right" && "text-right font-mono",
                  )}
                >
                  {c.render(row)}
                </td>
              ))}
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  );
}

export function Badge({
  children,
  color = "slate",
}: {
  children: ReactNode;
  color?: "slate" | "green" | "red" | "amber" | "indigo";
}): JSX.Element {
  const colors: Record<string, string> = {
    slate: "bg-slate-100 text-slate-700",
    green: "bg-green-100 text-green-800",
    red: "bg-red-100 text-red-800",
    amber: "bg-amber-100 text-amber-800",
    indigo: "bg-indigo-100 text-indigo-800",
  };
  return (
    <span
      className={clsx(
        "inline-flex items-center rounded px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium",
        colors[color],
      )}
    >
      {children}
    </span>
  );
}

export function Empty({ children }: { children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element {
  return (
    <div className="rounded border border-dashed border-slate-300 px-4 py-6 text-center text-sm text-slate-500">
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

export function Spinner(): JSX.Element {
  return (
    <div className="inline-block h-4 w-4 animate-spin rounded-full border-2 border-slate-300 border-t-slate-600" />
  );
}

export function Modal({
  open,
  onClose,
  children,
}: {
  open: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
  children: ReactNode;
}): JSX.Element | null {
  if (!open) return null;
  return (
    <div
      className="fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center bg-black/50"
      onClick={onClose}
    >
      <div
        className="max-w-lg rounded-lg bg-white p-6 shadow-lg"
        onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
      >
        {children}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export function Toast({ message }: { message: string }): JSX.Element {
  return (
    <div className="fixed bottom-4 right-4 rounded bg-slate-900 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white shadow-lg">
      {message}
    </div>
  );
}

```

```typescript
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Card, Empty, Spinner, Table, Badge } from "../ui";
import { db, type Project, type Competition, type AgentJob, type HumanDecision } from "../lib/db";

function Pill({ status }: { status: string }): JSX.Element {
  const color =
    status === "approved" || status === "succeeded"
      ? "green"
      : status === "rejected" || status === "failed"
        ? "red"
        : status === "pending" || status === "paused" || status === "running" || status === "queued"
          ? "amber"
          : "slate";
  return <Badge color={color}>{status}</Badge>;
}

export function Dashboard(): JSX.Element {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [projects, setProjects] = useState<Project[]>([]);
  const [competitions, setCompetitions] = useState<Competition[]>([]);
  const [jobs, setJobs] = useState<AgentJob[]>([]);
  const [decisions, setDecisions] = useState<HumanDecision[]>([]);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    (async () => {
      try {
        const [p, c, j, d] = await Promise.all([
          db.listProjects(),
          db.listCompetitions(),
          db.listInflightJobs(),
          db.listRecentDecisions(10),
        ]);
        if (!live) return;
        setProjects(p);
        setCompetitions(c);
        setJobs(j);
        setDecisions(d);
      } catch (e) {
        if (live) setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e));
      } finally {
        if (live) setLoading(false);
      }
    })();
    return () => {
      live = false;
    };
  }, []);

  if (loading) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-slate-500">
        <Spinner />
        Loading dashboard…
      </div>
    );
  }
  if (error) {
    return <Empty>Failed to load: {error}</Empty>;
  }

  return (
    <div className="space-y-6">
      <Card title="Projects">
        {projects.length === 0 ? (
          <Empty>No projects yet.</Empty>
        ) : (
          <div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3">
            {projects.map((p) => (
              <div
                key={p.id}
                className="rounded border border-slate-200 p-3"
              >
                <h3 className="font-semibold">{p.name}</h3>
                <p className="text-xs text-slate-500">{p.kind ?? "general"}</p>
                <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-slate-600">{p.description}</p>
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
        )}
      </Card>

      <Card title="Active competitions">
        <Table
          rows={competitions}
          columns={[
            { key: "slug", header: "Slug", render: (c) => c.slug },
            { key: "title", header: "Name", render: (c) => c.title ?? "—" },
            {
              key: "repo",
              header: "Repo",
              render: (c) =>
                c.repo_url ? (
                  <a
                    className="text-indigo-700 hover:underline"
                    href={c.repo_url}
                    target="_blank"
                    rel="noopener noreferrer"
                  >
                    {c.repo_url}
                  </a>
                ) : (
                  "—"
                ),
            },
            { key: "platform", header: "Platform", render: (c) => c.platform },
          ]}
          empty={<Empty>No active competitions.</Empty>}
        />
      </Card>

      <Card title="Inflight runs">
        <Table
          rows={jobs}
          columns={[
            { key: "id", header: "Job", render: (j) => j.id.slice(0, 8) },
            { key: "model", header: "Model", render: (j) => j.model ?? "—" },
            {
              key: "status",
              header: "Status",
              render: (j) => <Pill status={j.status} />,
            },
            {
              key: "started_at",
              header: "Started",
              render: (j) => j.started_at?.slice(0, 19) ?? "—",
            },
            {
              key: "turns",
              header: "Turns",
              align: "right",
              render: (j) => j.turns_used ?? 0,
            },
            {
              key: "cost",
              header: "Cost ($)",
              align: "right",
              render: (j) => (j.cost_usd ?? 0).toFixed(4),
            },
          ]}
          empty={<Empty>No inflight runs.</Empty>}
        />
      </Card>

      <Card title="Recent decisions">
        <Table
          rows={decisions}
          columns={[
            {
              key: "type",
              header: "Operation",
              render: (d) => d.decision_type,
            },
            {
              key: "status",
              header: "Status",
              render: (d) => <Pill status={d.status} />,
            },
            {
              key: "requested_by",
              header: "By",
              render: (d) => d.requested_by ?? "—",
            },
            {
              key: "created",
              header: "Requested",
              render: (d) => d.created_at.slice(0, 19),
            },
          ]}
          empty={<Empty>No decisions recorded.</Empty>}
        />
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}

```

```typescript
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Link } from "react-router-dom";
import { Card, Empty, Spinner, Table, Badge } from "../ui";
import { db, type AgentJob } from "../lib/db";

export function Runs(): JSX.Element {
  const [jobs, setJobs] = useState<AgentJob[]>([]);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);

  useEffect(() => {
    db.listRecentRuns(50)
      .then(setJobs)
      .finally(() => setLoading(false));
  }, []);

  if (loading) return <Spinner />;

  return (
    <Card title="Recent runs">
      <Table
        rows={jobs}
        columns={[
          {
            key: "id",
            header: "Job",
            render: (j) => (
              <Link
                to={`/runs/${j.id}`}
                className="text-indigo-700 hover:underline"
              >
                {j.id.slice(0, 8)}
              </Link>
            ),
          },
          {
            key: "status",
            header: "Status",
            render: (j) => <Badge>{j.status}</Badge>,
          },
          { key: "model", header: "Model", render: (j) => j.model ?? "—" },
          {
            key: "turns",
            header: "Turns",
            align: "right",
            render: (j) => j.turns_used ?? 0,
          },
          {
            key: "cost",
            header: "Cost ($)",
            align: "right",
            render: (j) => (j.cost_usd ?? 0).toFixed(4),
          },
          {
            key: "created",
            header: "Created",
            render: (j) => j.created_at.slice(0, 19),
          },
        ]}
        empty={<Empty>No runs.</Empty>}
      />
    </Card>
  );
}
```
